> 井。改邑不改井，無喪無得，往來井井。汔至，亦未繘井，羸其瓶，凶。

Hexagram 48 is about a well, and its first four characters are the whole idea.

## 井 is a pictograph of the well-head

A pictograph: the ring of wooden rails at the mouth of a well.

說文 says 八家一井 — eight households to one well. That is the well-field system, and it is an institution borrowing the character's name. It is not the character's original sense.

So a correction, in the family of the previous chapters: 井 is not 會意. It was not drawn from the idea "eight families around a well." A shape existed first, and the character came from the shape.

Pictographs read as pictures-with-a-message is the neighbouring fault to phonetics read as pictures. This book logs it here.

## 改邑不改井

邑: the walled town, the fief.

改邑 has two readings: the fief being reassigned, or the settlement moving.

Both work, and the point is the same: the well belongs to the ground, not to the people.

People can leave. The ground cannot be moved. Which makes the well the one thing that group cannot carry away with them.

## 汔至，亦未繘井，羸其瓶

汔: nearly. The water is nearly at the lip of the well.

繘: the rope for drawing water. 未繘井 — the rope has not finished being hauled.

羸: to ruin, to break. 羸其瓶 — the pitcher is smashed.

Not "the pitcher leaked." The whole trip is wasted, at the last moment, with the water almost up.

凶. Which is the most exact anxiety in the book: not failing early, failing at 99 percent.

## 井渫不食

九三 井渫不食，為我心惻；可用汲，王明，並受其福.

渫: to dredge out the silt, to make the water clear.

The well has been cleaned and nobody drinks from it. 為我心惻 — it grieves me.

可用汲 — it could be drawn from. 王明 — if the king were bright, everyone would receive the benefit.

Which is the most naked line in the hexagram: the competence is there, the water is clean, and the only missing thing is the one who would notice. And the line does not pretend that is a moral failing of the water.

## 井甃

六四 井甃，無咎.

甃: to line with brick or stone.

The only line in the book that is about maintaining infrastructure, and its verdict is exactly 無咎 — no fault. Not good fortune. No fault. Which is the honest reward for repair work.

## 井冽，寒泉食

九五: the well is clear and cold, and the cold spring is drunk from.

冽: clear and cold.

At the ruler's place, the well is simply good water. No argument, no merit — the thing works.

## 勿幕

上六 井收勿幕，有孚元吉.

收 has two readings: the drawing finished, or the well-head built up to a narrow mouth. 幕: to cover.

勿幕 — do not cover it.

Both readings land on the same sense: the mouth is open, and anyone may come.

## 勞民勸相

The 象: 君子以勞民勸相.

勞 is to encourage and to give rest to; 相 is to help.

相 here is not "to look at one another." It is 相助 — mutual aid.

Read as "encourage the people to look at each other," the sentence is unsayable. Read as "encourage the people to help each other," it is the virtue of the well: water nourishes people, and people nourish people.

## The test

Take a shared resource you depend on — a standard, a dataset, a building, a piece of institutional knowledge. Ask the hexagram's first question: is this movable or fixed? Then the second: has anyone cleaned it lately, and is anyone drinking?
